name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q01 - Preservation of pollen grains as fossils

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Pollen grains are well-preserved as fossils.

Reason (R): The outer wall (exine) of pollen grains is made up of sporopollenin, which is resistant to high temperatures, strong acids, alkali, and enzymatic degradation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollen grains have a prominent two-layered wall consisting of a hard outer exine and a thin inner intine. The chemical composition of the exine determines the durability of the pollen grain in the environment.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion states that pollen grains are well-preserved as fossils. This statement is correct because pollen grains can survive harsh geological conditions over long periods without decaying.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason states that the exine is composed of sporopollenin, which withstands high temperatures, strong acids, and alkalis, and has no known enzyme capable of degrading it. This statement is also correct.

Step 4: Relationship Check
Because sporopollenin is one of the most resistant organic materials known and resists physical, chemical, and biological degradation, it directly prevents the decay of pollen grains, enabling their preservation as fossils. Therefore, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): The innermost wall layer of a microsporangium, the tapetum, nourishes the developing pollen grains.

Reason (R): Cells of the tapetum possess scanty cytoplasm and are strictly uninucleate throughout anther development.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A typical microsporangium is surrounded by four wall layers: the epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and the innermost tapetum. While the outer three layers provide protection and aid in anther dehiscence, the tapetum has a nutritive role.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion states that the tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium and nourishes the developing pollen grains. This statement is completely correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason claims that tapetal cells possess scanty cytoplasm and are strictly uninucleate. This is incorrect because, to perform their active nutritive function, cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally contain more than one nucleus.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is correct, whereas the Reason is incorrect.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q03 - Chasmogamous and cleistogamous flowers in autogamy

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Chasmogamous flowers do not open at all and are therefore invariably autogamous.

Reason (R): In cleistogamous flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other, so pollen grains come in contact with the stigma when anthers dehisce in the flower buds, ensuring seed-set even without pollinators.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plants such as Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina produce two distinct types of flowers: chasmogamous flowers and cleistogamous flowers.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion states that chasmogamous flowers do not open at all and are invariably autogamous. This statement is incorrect because chasmogamous flowers are normal flowers that open and expose their anthers and stigma, making complete autogamy rather rare in them. It is cleistogamous flowers that do not open at all.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason accurately describes cleistogamous flowers: their anthers and stigma lie close together inside the unopened bud, leading to self-pollination upon anther dehiscence and assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators. This statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is incorrect, whereas the Reason is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q04 - Organisation of mature angiosperm embryo sac

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): A typical angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8-nucleate and 7-celled.

Reason (R): The filiform apparatus present at the micropylar tip of the synergids guides the entry of the pollen tube into the synergid.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The female gametophyte (embryo sac) develops from a functional megaspore through three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions, followed by cell wall formation and cellular organisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. After the 8-nucleate stage, six nuclei are enclosed by cell walls to form three cells of the egg apparatus (two synergids and one egg cell) at the micropylar end and three antipodal cells at the chalazal end. The remaining two polar nuclei lie in a single large central cell, resulting in a 7-celled, 8-nucleate mature embryo sac.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is also correct. The synergids possess special cellular thickenings at their micropylar tip called the filiform apparatus, which plays an important role in guiding the pollen tube into the synergid.

Step 4: Relationship Check
Although both statements are factually true about the mature embryo sac, the role of the filiform apparatus in guiding the pollen tube does not explain why the embryo sac has 8 nuclei arranged into 7 cells (which is due to free-nuclear divisions and two polar nuclei sharing one central cell).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, but the Reason is NOT the correct explanation of the Assertion.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q05 - Pollination mechanisms in aquatic flowering plants

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): All aquatic flowering plants use water as the pollinating agent to achieve fertilisation.

Reason (R): In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the surface of water by a long stalk and pollen grains are released onto the surface of water to be carried passively by water currents.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollination by water is quite rare in angiosperms and is restricted to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons such as Vallisneria, Hydrilla, and marine sea-grasses like Zostera.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion states that all aquatic flowering plants use water for pollination. This is incorrect because in a majority of aquatic plants, such as water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the water level and are pollinated by insects or wind just like land plants.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason describes epihydrophily in Vallisneria, where the female flower reaches the water surface via a long stalk and male flowers or pollen grains are released onto the water surface to drift passively with water currents until some reach the stigma. This statement is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is incorrect, whereas the Reason is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q06 - Outbreeding devices in monoecious and self-incompatible plants

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Monoecious plants such as castor and maize prevent autogamy but cannot prevent geitonogamy.

Reason (R): Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Flowering plants have evolved several outbreeding devices to discourage continued self-pollination and prevent inbreeding depression, including unisexuality (monoecy and dioecy) and self-incompatibility.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. In monoecious plants like castor and maize, separate male and female unisexual flowers are borne on the same plant. Since a flower is either male or female, pollen cannot transfer within the same flower (preventing autogamy), but pollen can still transfer from a male flower to a female flower on the same plant (allowing geitonogamy).

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is also correct. Self-incompatibility is indeed a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from the same flower or other flowers of the same plant from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth.

Step 4: Relationship Check
The two statements describe two independent outbreeding devices. The mechanism of self-incompatibility does not explain why monoecious plants prevent autogamy while permitting geitonogamy (which is explained by the presence of both male and female unisexual flowers on the same plant).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, but the Reason is NOT the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Emasculation is not required when the female parent in an artificial hybridisation experiment produces unisexual flowers.

Reason (R): Unisexual female flowers lack a stigma, so they cannot receive unwanted pollen before bagging.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Artificial hybridisation uses emasculation and bagging to ensure that only desired pollen grains pollinate the stigma and to prevent contamination from unwanted pollen.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. Emasculation is the removal of anthers from a bisexual flower bud before dehiscence. When the female parent produces unisexual (pistillate) flowers, anthers are already absent, so there is no need for emasculation.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is incorrect. Unisexual female flowers do possess a functional stigma, style, and ovary; they only lack stamens (anthers). Because they have a stigma that can receive unwanted pollen, the female flower buds must still be bagged before opening until the stigma becomes receptive.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is correct, whereas the Reason is incorrect.

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In angiosperms, endosperm development precedes embryo development, and most zygotes divide only after a certain amount of endosperm is formed.

Reason (R): The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to form a triploid endosperm tissue filled with reserve food materials that provides assured nutrition to the developing embryo.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Following double fertilisation, the primary endosperm cell (PEC) develops into the endosperm, while the diploid zygote develops into the embryo.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. In flowering plants, endosperm formation always precedes embryogeny, and the zygote remains dormant for some time until sufficient endosperm has formed.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is also correct. The primary endosperm cell divides repeatedly to produce a triploid endosperm tissue whose cells are packed with reserve food materials to nourish the developing embryo.

Step 4: Relationship Check
The delay in zygote division until a certain amount of endosperm is formed is specifically an adaptive strategy to ensure that the developing embryo has an assured supply of nutrition from the endosperm tissue. Thus, the Reason directly explains the Assertion.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q09 - Double fertilisation and coconut endosperm types

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Double fertilisation is an event unique to flowering plants, involving both syngamy and triple fusion within the embryo sac.

Reason (R): Coconut water from a tender coconut represents free-nuclear endosperm made up of thousands of nuclei, whereas the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Double fertilisation is a hallmark of angiosperms, and the resulting primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) undergoes characteristic nuclear and cellular divisions during endosperm development.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. Inside the embryo sac, one male gamete fuses with the egg cell (syngamy) to form a diploid zygote, and the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion) to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus. Together, these two fusion events constitute double fertilisation, which is unique to flowering plants.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is also correct. In the common mode of endosperm development, the PEN undergoes successive free-nuclear divisions followed by cellularisation. In tender coconut, the coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm (thousands of nuclei) and the surrounding white kernel is cellular endosperm.

Step 4: Relationship Check
While both statements are accurate, the structure of coconut water and white kernel illustrates post-fertilisation endosperm development rather than explaining why double fertilisation (syngamy plus triple fusion) is unique to flowering plants.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, but the Reason is NOT the correct explanation of the Assertion.

answer.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q10 - Monocot embryo parts and non-albuminous seeds

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): In the grass family, the single cotyledon is called the coleoptile, which encloses the radicle and root cap at the lower end of the embryonal axis.

Reason (R): In non-albuminous seeds such as pea and groundnut, the endosperm is completely consumed during embryo development before seed maturation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Monocotyledonous embryos possess a single cotyledon and specialised protective sheaths around the shoot apex and radicle, while mature seeds are classified as albuminous or non-albuminous based on residual endosperm.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is incorrect on two counts: in the grass family, the single lateral cotyledon is called the scutellum (not coleoptile); the sheath enclosing the radicle and root cap is the coleorrhiza, whereas the coleoptile is a hollow foliar structure enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is correct. Non-albuminous (ex-albuminous) seeds, such as those of pea and groundnut, retain no residual endosperm because it is completely consumed by the developing embryo prior to seed maturation.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is incorrect, whereas the Reason is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q11 - Distinction between false fruits and parthenocarpic fruits

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Apple and strawberry are classified as false fruits rather than true fruits.

Reason (R): False fruits develop without fertilisation, so they are always seedless.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Fruits are classified as true or false based on which floral parts contribute to fruit formation, and as parthenocarpic when they develop without fertilisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. True fruits develop solely from the ovary, whereas in species such as apple, strawberry, and cashew, the thalamus also contributes to fruit formation. Therefore, apple and strawberry are called false fruits.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is incorrect. Fruits that develop without fertilisation and are seedless (such as banana) are called parthenocarpic fruits, not false fruits. False fruits such as apple are formed after fertilisation and contain seeds.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The Assertion is correct, whereas the Reason is incorrect.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_AR_Q12 - Application of apomixis in hybrid seed industry

questiontext.text:
Assertion (A): Making hybrid varieties into apomicts would allow farmers to use hybrid seeds year after year without having to buy new hybrid seeds every season.

Reason (R): In apomictic hybrids, embryos develop without fertilisation and reduction division, so there is no segregation of characters in the hybrid progeny.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction by producing seeds without fertilisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion
The Assertion is correct. Normally, farmers must purchase expensive hybrid seeds every year because seeds saved from hybrid crops segregate and lose hybrid vigour. Converting hybrids into apomicts eliminates the need to buy new hybrid seeds annually.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Reason
The Reason is also correct. In apomixis, diploid embryos form without meiotic reduction division and fertilisation, which prevents genetic segregation of traits in the progeny.

Step 4: Relationship Check
Because apomixis prevents segregation of characters in the progeny, the desirable hybrid traits are faithfully maintained across generations. This directly explains why farmers can reuse seeds from apomictic hybrids year after year.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Both the Assertion and the Reason are correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
